ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Within the Caodong Five Ranks, the relative within the absolute (正中偏) names differentiated appearance within the absolute or upright. Records identify it relationally and then test it through verses, images, and contrast with the absolute within the relative (偏中正).
EvidenceBody: Caoshan Benji explains that the upright position is the empty realm and the partial position the realm of forms; he glosses the relative within the absolute (正中偏) as turning from principle toward affairs and elsewhere as the lord looking toward the minister. Hongzhi Zhengjue's Five Ranks verse gives the rank a night image in which a wooden boy strikes the moon's door and wakes a jade woman.

The Mirror of Humans and Devas records an unnamed monastic asking Fenyang Shanzhao for this rank and preserves Fenyang's moon-and-cock response. Langting Ting gives it swallows murmuring between roof beams. Juelang Daosheng relates it to an eastern circle and lesser yang, while Ruibai Mingxue identifies his own shout as this rank once he has mounted the seat. Tianran Hanshi transmits an older night-and-moon verse whose historical author is not established in the available six-rung evidence and then offers his own matching verse, showing that no single image exhausts the relation.

Senses.Note: Seven exact witnesses in seven independent works support one Five Ranks relation; the English target follows the conventional relational order while alternates preserve the Chinese pair's older upright/partial vocabulary.

Occurrences.Kwic: 正中偏，三更初夜月明前。莫怪相逢不相識，隱隱猶懷昔日嫌。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Tianran of Lushan (廬山天然禪師語錄): the headword speaker is an unnamed historical author of the original Five Ranks stanza; the formula “the original verse says” (原頌曰) marks this as an older quoted stanza, but the line, expanded context, section heading, book title, TEI metadata, and available parallel-witness check do not securely name its historical author. Tianran Hanshi is the later quoter and author of the separate response introduced as “the matching verse says” (和曰), not this headword-bearing original stanza.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: the formula “the original verse says” (原頌曰) introduces the headword-bearing older stanza; the later formula “the matching verse says” (和曰) introduces Tianran Hanshi's separate matching verse.

DraftActorProof.GrammaticalSubject: The historical author of the stanza introduced by the formula “the original verse says” (原頌曰); no secure personal name is established in the available evidence.
DraftActorProof.FullCaseDecision: A reviewed-unnamed historical verse-author owns the original headword stanza; Tianran owns the later quotation frame and separate response introduced as “the matching verse says” (和曰).

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: A compact relational rank is repeatedly made visible through paired direction, night imagery, birds, diagrams, and the timing of a shout.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The seven witnesses use incompatible surface images, and later records dispute diagrammatic and directional explanations; no one image or later schema can replace the relational rank name.

DifferentThingTest.Reason: Each explicitly labels the same first named relation in the Five Ranks sequence.

DraftEvidence.AliasRationale: Aliases include the conventional absolute-relative lookup and older upright-partial vocabulary without treating 偏 as moral bias.

ModifierControls.Finding: 中 marks one member appearing within the other; 正 and 偏 are paired relational terms, not moral praise and blame.

FamilyControls.Finding: The reverse nested relation and regular paired contrast, kept separate.
The rank system that supplies the lord-minister vocabulary and sequence.
